tagline: America's second-largest homebuilder (Miami): builds and sells single-family homes under the Lennar brand (about 80,000 deliveries a year at a ~$372K average price), plus mortgage and title services, multifamily and technology investments. Berkshire Hathaway crossed 10% ownership in September 2026.

notes: Lennar's strategy is to hold volume and cut prices: it used ~12% incentives in fiscal Q3 to keep selling 4.1 homes per community per month, so margins and earnings have fallen even as deliveries held near 21,000 a quarter.
Management said conditions 'deteriorated' during the quarter as the 30-year mortgage rate rose to ~6.8% and higher; new orders fell 9% and backlog is 16,857 homes ($6.3B).

Cost progress: construction cost per sq ft −6% YoY, record-low 116-day cycle time, and an asset-light land model (it owns under 2.5% of ~488,000 controlled homesites, much of it via spinoff Millrose Properties).

Berkshire bought 7.39M Class A and 114,832 Class B shares between Sep 17 and Oct 2 (about $595M by the Form 4 prices). A 13G/A dated Sep 30 shows 26.03M A shares, 12.5% of the class, and the Oct 2 total is 28.44M A.

Mortgage rates and the Fed path: Lennar's volume-first model is most sensitive to rates

bull.text: Berkshire has roughly tripled its stake since March to 28.4M A shares (~12.5%+ of the class), buying at $75–82, near today's price
Cheap on assets: price/book 0.85, P/E 14.5, 2.6% dividend and a 6.8% buyback yield
Lowest-cost producer mindset: build cost −6% YoY, record 116-day cycle time, asset-light land; US housing shortage remains

bear.text: Earnings in decline: TTM net income −51%, Q4 EPS guide $1.30–$1.65 vs $2.00 expected, FY26 deliveries cut
Analysts lean negative: consensus Sell, ~2% upside to the average target, several targets cut since the Q3 miss
Hunterbrook Media alleges sales to spinoff Millrose don't match the rent-to-own story told to investors; law firms are advertising a fraud investigation (allegations, not findings)
Rate-sensitive: management says conditions worsened with mortgage rates near 6.8%+; ~12% incentives to sustain volume

runContext.title: What kind of company this is, and is it on a Futura list?
runContext.summary: LEN is not a crypto miner, crypto-treasury company or commodity producer under Futura's rules. Its Nasdaq industry is 'Homebuilding' (Consumer Discretionary), which isn't on Early Inflection's COMMODITY_INDUSTRIES list, and it is not in MINERS or CRYPTO_TREASURY. It is on none of the lists today because its revenue and earnings are shrinking.

runContext.signalsTitle: Why it isn't on a list
signals: Risk It and Growth both start from revenue growth; Lennar's revenue fell in each of the last five quarters, so it doesn't pass either screen's first filters.

Early Inflection: it scores only 25 off-screen. It earns full marks for valuation (15/15) and for not having already run (10/10, −42% from its high), but zero for revenue acceleration, margin expansion, forward growth, trend and analysts.

The case for LEN is a value/contrarian one (Berkshire buying below book value at a cyclical low), which none of the current growth-oriented screens is built to catch. The Piotroski tab is the closest fit, but its F-Score is 4 of 9, short of the 8–9 bar.
runContext.caveat: This page doesn't change any screening rules; whether to add a value or 'smart-money buying' screen is your call.
